Title: Diagnosis of test `org.apache.commons.cli.PatternOptionBuilderTest.testExistingFilePattern()`

Details: 
The test `testExistingFilePattern` parses the pattern string `"g<"` using `PatternOptionBuilder.parsePattern`. This pattern indicates an option 'g' having an argument of a specific type denoted by '<'. According to the method `getValueClass(char)` in `PatternOptionBuilder`, the character '<' corresponds to `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE`, which is defined as `FileInputStream.class`. Hence, the option 'g' is configured to expect a `FileInputStream` argument.

The test then uses `PosixParser.parse` to parse command line options based on these options, providing `-g` with the value `"src/test/resources/existing-readable.file"`. The parsed argument object is retrieved using `line.getOptionObject("g")`. The method `getOptionObject` relies on `getParsedOptionValue` to convert the option value to the specified type.

The test asserts that the retrieved object for option 'g' should indeed be an instance of `FileInputStream`, which matches the linked type `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE`.

The failure of this test suggests that, although the option is declared with type `FileInputStream.class`, the actual object returned by `getOptionObject` is not a `FileInputStream`. This discrepancy likely arises from the internals of the parsing process (`PosixParser.parse`) or the conversion process (`getParsedOptionValue`), where the argument string for option 'g' is not properly converted to a `FileInputStream` despite the type hint.

Further investigation should focus on the parsing and value conversion steps within the `PosixParser` and `CommandLine` classes to ensure the argument string value is correctly transformed into an instance of the specified `FileInputStream` type.

Suggested methods to inspect or fix:
- org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[])
- org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue(java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
